newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsann Kuen sees better 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: Tsann Kuen sees better 1997 results.

text.p: Chinese appliance maker Tsann Kuen on Thursday published results showing a 45 percent growth in net profits, and an official said 1997 would see further progress.
Tsann Kuen has set a turnover target of $114 million for 1997 under international accounting standards, the Taiwan-invested company said in its 1996 annual report in Shenzhen-based Securities Times.

The company booked turnover of 971.42 million yuan (US$117.04 million) for 1996 under international standards, an official at the firm's finance department told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"But we are going to challenge the US$120 million mark for 1997," he said.
"We also expect 1997 net profit to beat the 1996 level," he said but declined to elaborate.
Under international standards, Tsann Kuen had net profit of 55.53 million yuan for 1996 compared with 38.39 million yuan in 1995, according to Tsann Kuen's 1996 and 1995 annual reports.
Based on Chinese accounting standards, the company booked turnover of 896.67 million yuan in 1996 against 784.09 million yuan in the previous year, the report said.
Net profit based on Chinese accounting standards reached 46.46 million yuan in 1996 against 35.88 million in 1995, it said.
Earnings per share were 0.24 yuan, unchanged from the 1995 level, it said.

The company's board of directors proposed to distribute a cash dividend of 0.50 yuan and one bonus share for every 10 shares based on 1996 profit, and a one-for-10 bonus issue based on capital surplus, the report said.
Tsann Kuen will present the dividend plan at a shareholders' meeting in Xiamen city on May 14, it said.
The company's shareholders will also vote on its plan to issue 40 million additional B shares and use the money to expand the company's sales network and help cash flow, it said.
The company has tentatively priced the issue at between HK$3.5 and HK$4.0 per share and aimed to make the offer by June this year, the official said without giving more details.
Tsann Kuen's B shares ended on Thursday at HK$4.37, up HK$0.27.
